scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The Akan label denotes related peoples, not one state or the whole population of Ghana. The imported polygons change markedly between 1500 and 1530; historical boundaries remain unverified.

Begho is a regional and multiethnic archaeological example. Its Brong and Mande quarters are not collapsed into one identity. The 1973 abstract supplies an approximate early site chronology; the 2015 abstract reports finds without object-by-object dates. Full subscription articles were not inspected.
The Met object is nineteenth to mid-twentieth century and has no excavated Begho provenance. Its collection number is not a production date.
The Met commentary’s erroneous late-eighteenth-century British-conquest statement is omitted. No disputed weight conversion or earliest-invention claim is required.

Kraamer’s article was published in 2006; the interpretive twentieth-century phase closes at 2007 to keep that contemporary account within its documented scope. Ewe weavers are not categorized as Akan.

The author-posted pottery text was read in full for the cited production sections. Mpraeso’s Kwahu identity is explicit in its study-area discussion. These observations are not backdated to medieval pottery.
UNESCO’s listing has inconsistent building counts; no count is repeated. Surviving ritual architecture is distinguished from all Akan architecture.
No single conquest is assigned to all Akan peoples, and no unverified successor is linked. Independent historical review and geometry assessment remain pending.
